The '''2022 Hackney London Borough Council election''' took place on 5 May 2022. All 57 members of [[Hackney London Borough Council]] were up for election. The elections took place alongside the election for the [[mayor of Hackney]], [[2022 London local elections|local elections in the other London boroughs]], and [[2022 United Kingdom local elections|elections to local authorities across the United Kingdom]].

The [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] retained overall control of the council. It won 50 of the 57 seats, losing two seats to the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]]. The [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] held the five seats that they had had before the election, remaining the official opposition.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Council election results {{!}} Hackney Council |url=https://hackney.gov.uk/council-elections/ |access-date=2022-05-06 |website=hackney.gov.uk}}</ref>

== Background ==

=== History ===
[[File:Hackney London UK local election 2018 map.svg|thumb|Result of the 2018 borough election]]
The thirty-two [[London boroughs]] were established in 1965 by the [[London Government Act 1963]]. They are the principal authorities in Greater London and have responsibilities including education, housing, planning, highways, social services, libraries, recreation, waste, environmental health and revenue collection. Some of the powers are shared with the [[Greater London Authority]], which also manages passenger transport, police and fire.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The essential guide to London local government {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/essential-guide-london-local-government|access-date=2021-10-10|website=Londoncouncils.gov.uk}}</ref>

Since its formation, Hackney has usually been under [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] control except for a period from 1968 to 1971 when it was under [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]] control and from 1998 to 2002 when it was under [[no overall control]]. Councillors have mostly been elected from the Labour Party, Conservative Party and [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]], with some [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] councillors being elected in 1998 and 2006. In the [[2018 Hackney London Borough Council election|most recent election in 2018]], the Liberal Democrats lost their three seats in the Cazenove ward with Labour winning 52 seats with 63.0% of the vote across the borough and the Conservatives winning the remaining 5 seats with 11.1% of the vote across the borough. The Green Party won 16.9% of the vote across the borough without winning any seats, performing best in the Dalston and Hackney Downs wards.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2018-05-04|title=Dalston Labour councillor re-elected by 21 votes after dramatic recount|url=https://www.hackneycitizen.co.uk/2018/05/04/dalston-labour-councillor-recount/|access-date=2021-10-10|website=Hackney Citizen|language=en-GB}}</ref> The Liberal Democrats won 8.6% of the vote without winning any seats, performing best in Cazenove ward. The council is run under a mayoral system, so its leader is the directly elected [[mayor of Hackney]]. The incumbent mayor of Hackney was Labour's [[Philip Glanville]], who had held that role since a 2016 by-election.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-09-16|title=Hackney elects Philip Glanville as mayor|url=https://www.hackneycitizen.co.uk/2016/09/16/hackney-elects-philip-glanville-mayor/|access-date=2021-10-10|website=Hackney Citizen|language=en-GB}}</ref>

In November 2021, the local Conservative Party in Hackney selected Oliver Hall as their candidate for Mayor. At nineteen years old, he is thought to have been the youngest ever major-party candidate for a directly elected mayoralty in England and Wales.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/OliverHallUK/status/1461419691768004608|title=Some news from me: I'm delighted to announce that I've been selected as the Conservative Party Candidate for Mayor of Hackney for the 2022 election!|website=Twitter.com|access-date=19 January 2022}}</ref>

=== Council term ===
A Labour councillor for [[Victoria (Hackney ward)|Victoria ward]], Alex Kuye, resigned in September 2018 for health reasons. A by-election to replace him was held in October 2018, which was won by the Labour candidate Penny Wrout with 58% of the vote against a swing to the Liberal Democrats.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Baston|first=Lewis|date=2018-10-22|title=Hackney by election: Labour hold Victoria ward, despite swing to Lib Dems|url=https://www.onlondon.co.uk/hackney-by-election-labour-hold-victoria-ward-despite-swing-to-lib-dems/|access-date=2021-10-10|website=OnLondon|language=en-GB}}</ref> Wrout taught journalism at the [[University of Essex]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bartholomew|first=Emma|date=2018-10-19|title=Victoria ward by-election: Labour's Penny Wrout wins landslide victory|url=https://www.hackneygazette.co.uk/news/penny-wrout-wins-victoria-ward-by-election-3605220|access-date=2021-10-10|website=Hackney Gazette|language=en-UK}}</ref> In November 2019, a Labour councillor for Clissold ward, Ned Hercock, resigned for personal reasons.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Gelder|first=Sam|date=2019-11-05|title=By-election called as Clissold ward Labour councillor resigns|url=https://www.hackneygazette.co.uk/news/local-council/by-election-called-as-clissold-ward-labour-councillor-resigns-3640824|access-date=2021-10-10|website=Hackney Gazette|language=en-UK}}</ref> A by-election was held on 12 December 2019 on the same date as the [[2019 United Kingdom general election|2019 general election]], which was won by the Labour candidate Kofo David.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Ed|last=Sheridan|date=2019-12-13|title=Labour's Kofo David elected as new councillor for Clissold ward by-election after Ned Hercock resigns|url=https://www.hackneygazette.co.uk/news/kofo-david-elected-as-clissold-ward-councillor-3646322|access-date=2021-10-10|website=Hackney Gazette|language=en-UK}}</ref> David was an activist training to be a barrister.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-11-14|title=Clissold ward: Meet the candidates for the by-election taking place on same day as general|url=https://www.hackneycitizen.co.uk/2019/11/14/clissold-ward-meet-candidates-by-election-taking-place-same-day-general/|access-date=2021-10-10|website=Hackney Citizen|language=en-GB}}</ref> His selection as the Labour candidate was criticised by opposing candidates who pointed to his unsuccessful court action against a former colleague who had accused him of sexual harassment and bullying.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-11-19|title=Selection of Labour by-election candidate questioned over historic harassment and bullying allegations|url=https://www.hackneycitizen.co.uk/2019/11/19/selection-of-labour-by-election-candidate-questioned-over-historic-harassment-and-bullying-allegations/|access-date=2021-10-10|website=Hackney Citizen|language=en-GB}}</ref>

[[Feryal Clark]], a Labour councillor for Hoxton East and Shoreditch, resigned after being elected as [[Member of Parliament (United Kingdom)|Member of Parliament]] (MP) for [[Enfield North (UK Parliament constituency)|Enfield North]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Chant|first=Holly|date=2021-04-28|title=All you need to know about the Hackney by-elections on May 6|url=https://www.hackneygazette.co.uk/news/local-council/hackney-by-election-candidates-for-may-6-7924268|access-date=2021-10-10|website=Hackney Gazette|language=en-UK}}</ref> A Labour councillor for King's Park, Tom Rahilly, resigned in March 2020 due to taking a politically restricted job.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-03-19|title=King's Park councillor to step down with by-election postponed to 2021|url=https://www.hackneycitizen.co.uk/2020/03/19/kings-park-councillor-step-down-election-postponed-2021/|access-date=2021-10-10|website=Hackney Citizen|language=en-GB}}</ref> A Conservative councillor for Stamford Hill West, Aron Klein, resigned in July 2020 due to ill health.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Ldrs|first=Ed Sheridan|date=2020-07-02|title=Stamford Hill Conservative councillor Aron Klein resigns for health reasons|url=https://www.hackneygazette.co.uk/news/stamford-hill-councillor-aron-klein-resigns-3665724|access-date=2021-10-10|website=Hackney Gazette|language=en-UK}}</ref> Jon Burke, a Labour councillor for Woodberry Down, resigned in January 2021 due to plans to move out of London.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Chant|first=Holly|date=2021-01-05|title=Hackney's Cllr Jon Burke resigns with ambitions to move north|url=https://www.hackneygazette.co.uk/news/local-council/hackney-environment-chief-resigns-6883948|access-date=2021-10-10|website=Hackney Gazette|language=en-UK}}</ref> Due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], all four by-elections were not held until May 2021 alongside the [[2021 London mayoral election]] and [[2021 London Assembly election|London Assembly election]]. The candidates for the incumbent party won in all four seats. The Labour candidate Anya Sizer won in Hoxton East and Shoreditch, with the Green Party coming second.<ref name=byresults>{{Cite web|first=Ed|last=Sheridan|date=2021-05-07|title=Hackney by-election results revealed|url=https://www.hackneygazette.co.uk/news/local-council/election-2021-hackney-by-election-results-7957128|access-date=2021-10-10|website=Hackney Gazette|language=en-UK}}</ref> The Labour candidate Lynne Troughton won in King's Park, with the Greens again coming second.<ref name=byresults /> The Conservative candidate Stephen Lisser won the Stamford Hill West by-election, with Labour coming a closer second.<ref name=byresults /> The Labour candidate Sarah Young won the Woodberry Down by-election with the Green Party coming in second place.<ref name=byresults />

Unlike most London boroughs, Hackney kept its existing ward boundaries, as they were last reviewed in 2013.

== Electoral process ==
Hackney, like other London borough councils, elects all of its councillors at once every four years. The previous election took place in 2018. The election took place by multi-member [[first-past-the-post voting]], with each ward being represented by two or three councillors. Electors had as many votes as there were councillors to be elected in their ward, with the top two or three being elected.

All [[Elections in the United Kingdom#Registration procedure|registered electors]] ([[British citizen|British]], [[Irish citizen|Irish]], [[Commonwealth citizen|Commonwealth]] and [[European Union]] citizens) living in London aged 18 or over were entitled to vote in the election. People who lived at two addresses in different councils, such as university students with different term-time and holiday addresses, were entitled to be registered for and vote in elections in both local authorities.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=How the elections work {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/london-elections/how-elections-work|access-date=2021-09-14|website=Londoncouncils.gov.uk}}</ref> Voting in-person at polling stations took place from 7:00 to 22:00 on election day, and voters were able to apply for postal votes or proxy votes in advance of the election.<ref name=":1" />

== Campaign ==

=== Mayoral election ===
The Conservatives selected the nineteen-year-old law student, Oliver Hall, as their mayoral candidate. Hall said he would stop any new [[Low Traffic Neighbourhood]] schemes and consult on removing existing ones. He also promised to build more affordable housing.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Julia |last=Gregory|date=2022-02-22 |title=Conservative mayoral candidate to scrap LTNs if elected |url=https://www.hackneygazette.co.uk/news/local-council/hackney-conservative-mayoral-candidate-oliver-hall-8708812 |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=Hackney Gazette |language=en-UK}}</ref> Gwenton Sloley, an anti-gang activist, stood as an independent candidate under the slogan "Hackney People Before Profit". He said that the proceeds of the crime fund should be spent on "talking therapy and drop-in services" to "help people whose mental health has deteriorated during successive lockdowns". He said he would work to stop children from being excluded from school, and provide mentoring to young people after they are arrested, to prevent them from getting involved in gangs and criminal activity.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-02-28 |title='It takes lives - same as the pandemic': Anti-gang activist puts crime prevention at forefront of mayoral bid |url=https://www.hackneycitizen.co.uk/2022/02/28/anti-gang-activist-crime-covid-recovery-mayoral-bid/ |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=Hackney Citizen |language=en-GB}}</ref>
